statement: The function returns a result r. Define a valid jump from i to j (0 <= i < j < n) to mean: either (nums[i] <= nums[j] and for every k with i < k < j, nums[k] < nums[i]) or (nums[i] > nums[j] and for every k with i < k < j, nums[k] >= nums[i]). Define a valid path from 0 to n-1 to be a finite sequence p_0,...,p_m with m >= 0, p_0 = 0, p_m = n-1, p_t < p_{t+1} for every 0 <= t < m, and every consecutive pair p_t -> p_{t+1} is a valid jump; its cost is sum_{t=1}^{m} costs[p_t], with the empty sum 0 when m=0. Then r is the minimum cost among all valid paths from 0 to n-1: equivalently, there exists a valid path P from 0 to n-1 with cost(P)=r, and every valid path Q from 0 to n-1 has cost(Q) >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume n = 1, so len(nums)=1 and len(costs)=1, with 0 <= nums[0] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[0] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= costs[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= sum_{i=1}^{n-1} costs[i], where the sum is 0 when n=1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = costs[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 2 <= n <= 100000 and all nums[i], costs[i] are in [0,100000]. Assume that a valid jump from 0 to n-1 exists, meaning either (nums[0] <= nums[n-1] and for every k with 0 < k < n-1, nums[k] < nums[0]) or (nums[0] > nums[n-1] and for every k with 0 < k < n-1, nums[k] >= nums[0]).

statement: The function returns a result r and r = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} costs[i], where the sum is 0 when n=1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and all nums[i], costs[i] are in [0,100000]. Assume nums is nondecreasing: for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, nums[i] <= nums[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r. For every c with 0 <= c <= 100000, let costs' be any slice of length n such that costs'[0] = c and costs'[i] = costs[i] for every i with 1 <= i < n. Whenever min_cost(nums, costs') returns a result r', we have r' = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r. Define a valid jump from i to j (0 <= i < j < n) to mean: either (nums[i] <= nums[j] and for every k with i < k < j, nums[k] < nums[i]) or (nums[i] > nums[j] and for every k with i < k < j, nums[k] >= nums[i]). Let J be the minimum number of jumps m over all finite sequences p_0,...,p_m with p_0=0, p_m=n-1, p_t < p_{t+1} for every 0 <= t < m, and every consecutive pair a valid jump. Then r = c * J.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and all nums[i], costs[i] are in [0,100000]. Assume there is c with 0 <= c <= 100000 such that costs[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r. Define a valid jump from i to j (0 <= i < j < n) to mean: either (nums[i] <= nums[j] and for every k with i < k < j, nums[k] < nums[i]) or (nums[i] > nums[j] and for every k with i < k < j, nums[k] >= nums[i]). Then there exists a finite sequence p_0,...,p_m with m >= 0, p_0=0, p_m=n-1, p_t < p_{t+1} for every 0 <= t < m, every p_t -> p_{t+1} a valid jump, and sum_{t=1}^{m} costs[p_t] = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r. For every finite sequence p_0,...,p_m with m >= 0, p_0=0, p_m=n-1, p_t < p_{t+1} for every 0 <= t < m, and every consecutive pair p_t -> p_{t+1} being a valid jump (defined as: either nums[p_t] <= nums[p_{t+1}] and for every k with p_t < k < p_{t+1}, nums[k] < nums[p_t], or nums[p_t] > nums[p_{t+1}] and for every k with p_t < k < p_{t+1}, nums[k] >= nums[p_t]), we have sum_{t=1}^{m} costs[p_t] >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(costs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= costs[i] <= 100000.
